subject: Dedicated capacity: surge tempo, prewarm obligations & amendment next steps
messages:
From: Eliot Barnes <eliot@umbrellasoft.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — Q4 launch surge needs

Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our engineering and ops teams: the product team expects a coordinated traffic spike for our Q4 launch around Nov 10–14. We need guidance on how Redwood would handle a short high-concurrency window (~2–4 hours) that could be 2–3x our baseline reserved TPS.

Specifically:
- Can you outline what prewarm windows you recommend for an event of this scale?
- How does Redwood bill for transient burst beyond the reserved slab (per-token vs flat uplift)?
- Any gating (eviction) behavior we should design for in our fallbacks?

We want to lock in numbers to feed procurement and legal but can be flexible on exact commit timing if Redwood can provide a short-run surge plan + amendment.

Appreciate a short plan and next steps by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Cheers,
Eliot Barnes
Head of Platform, UmbrellaSoft
E: eliot@umbrellasoft.com
T: +1 415 555 0132

Attachment: umbrella_capacity_estimate_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Barnes <eliot@umbrellasoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Aug 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — Q4 launch surge needs

Eliot — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary of a recommended approach we can move to amendment: 

1) Baseline reserved slab: confirm current commit (we have 120 reserved GPUs in the draft).
2) Shoulder prewarm: we recommend a 30–90 minute prewarm window depending on model statefulness and cold-start behavior; for your workload I suggest 45 minutes standard.
3) Short burst policy (temporary surge): up to 3x baseline for a 2-hour continuous period or two 1-hour windows inside a 24-hour day.
4) Billing for burst: default is usage-based per-token/on-demand rate for ephemeral capacity with a negotiated uplift cap (we can cap burst billing at 1.6x standard on-demand unit price for this deal).
5) Credits & grace: include 8 hours of surge credits per quarter to cover an agreed number of short windows (applies before billing kicks in).
6) Eviction & fallback: eviction priority will be pre-configured to drain ephemeral workloads first and fallback to lighter model variants or queued requests; we propose an ordered eviction list (ephemeral jobs -> async batches -> reserved interactive).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to add the surge caps and credit language to the proforma and draft amendment.
- Karthik to confirm autoscale triggers (metrics & percentiles) and eviction sequencing.
- I’ll share a short runbook for prewarm and live ops triggers.

I attached a concise runbook and a provisional capacity schedule to start procurement conversations. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize wording.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 4102

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 08 Aug 2028 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — Q4 launch surge needs

On Wed, Aug 8, 2028 at 1:04 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I attached a concise runbook and a provisional capacity schedule to start procurement conversations.

Thanks — a few technical clarifications I want captured in the amendment and runbook so ops and SREs align during the event: 
- Autoscale trigger: use a combination of 95th percentile token throughput and P95 tail latency breach for 3 continuous minutes to trigger ephemeral spin-up.
- Prewarm signal: allow an explicit API call from Umbrella ops to start prewarm (recommended) in addition to metric-driven prewarm. We can mark that call as billable only if prewarm completes and is used.
- Eviction priority: ephemeral nodes first, then spot-like slab (if any), then reserved. We will expose a per-instance priority tag to your team so you can mark critical job types.
- Fallback model variants: define three tiers (full-precision baseline, quantized-high, quantized-fast). We will auto-failover to quantized-fast for <100ms longer tail latency to preserve throughput.

I’ll prepare the autoscale parameters table and drop it into the Drive link Sergio shared. Also, note that ephemeral spin-up on our infra for warm models typically takes 6–12 minutes; for cold models budget 30–45 minutes which is why the 45-minute prewarm suggestion is conservative.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — Q4 launch surge needs

Eliot — looping in commercial detail. Per Sergio/Karthik’s recommendations, I drafted proforma commercial terms for the burst windows:

- Surge cap: up to 3x reserved for up to 2 hours continuous or split as two 1-hour windows in a 24h period.
- Billing: burst usage billed at on-demand unit price with a negotiated cap (max 1.6x on-demand) beyond the included surge credits.
- Surge credits: UmbrellaSoft receives 8 free surge credit hours per quarter; credits are applied before billing and do not roll beyond quarter boundary.
- Amendments: We’ll deliver a short-form amendment to your MSA that includes the prewarm obligations, autoscale triggers, and credit carve-out. Amendment turnaround target: 5 business days after signoff.

I attached the proforma capacity schedule (spreadsheet) and a redlined amendment stub for your legal team to review. If that all looks good, we’ll convert to a DocuSign-ready amendment and route to procurement.

If helpful, I can host a 45-minute commercial + ops call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk legal and SRE through the draft.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 312 555 2210
